ownership_reason: Only the gold sees each character together with the result of its HTML 4.0 entity lookup; hops 1-4 hold the whole String or char array and the buffer. The gold never writes '&' followed by '#' (every '&' it writes starts an entity name, and a raw '&' of the input becomes &), so no change of the input above the gold can make a numeric reference appear, and once the gold has appended a character unchanged no caller can tell it from the characters that needed no escaping without escaping the text again. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the sibling overload StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml(Writer, String), whose javadoc carries the same first sentence ('Escapes the characters in a String using HTML entities'), delegates to Entities.HTML40.escape, which writes '&#' code ';' for a character above 0x7F that has no entity name; StringEscapeUtils.escapeXml documents the same step ('unicode characters greater than 0x7f are currently escaped to their numerical \u equivalent') and testEscapeXml asserts "¡" for \u00A1; testUnescapeHtml reads the same htmlEscapes table the other way and decodes 日本語 and €Ÿ. The gold's javadoc promises, in the words of Entities.escape ('Escapes the characters in the String passed and writes the result'), to escape the characters of the array, which in this library includes those numeric references; the variant leaves \u65E5\u672C\u8A9E unescaped.
